item.title: Cold Turkey
item.description: Overview “Cold turkey” is an informal phrase that references attempts to quit substance use suddenly at once rather than gradually reducing usage over time.

item.title: Communities Mobilizing for Change on Alcohol (CMCA)
item.description: Overview Communities Mobilizing for Change on Alcohol (CMCA) describes a community-level public health intervention aimed at reducing underage drinking by shaping institutional practices and local social norms.

item.title: Corporate Political Activities (CPAs)
item.description: Overview Corporate Political Activities (CPAs) refer to strategies that companies use to shape the political, legal, and social environment that are considered outside the scope of market strategies or business decisions.

item.title: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
item.description: Overview Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is a term that describes the arguments that large corporations have become one of the dominant structures of social organization and so they are obligated to be aligned with the social values of the communities they operate in.

item.title: Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA)
item.description: Overview A cost-benefit analysis (CBA) is a decision-making tool that finds the difference between what is gained and what is lost in a decision.

item.title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis (CEA)
item.description: Overview A cost-effectiveness analysis is a tool to judge the impact of a policy or decision relative to the costs incurred in enacting it.

item.title: Counseling
item.description: Overview According to the American Psychological Association, counseling refers to: “professional assistance in coping with personal problems, including emotional, behavioral, vocational, marital, educational, rehabilitation, and life-stage (e.g., retirement) problems.

item.title: Crack Baby
item.description: Overview The term “crack baby” is a derogatory reference to babies who were exposed to cocaine as fetuses, which emerged as part of the general hysteria over the crack epidemic in the United States during the 1980s onward.
